newsitem.title: USA: "Lost World" tramples on U.S. box office rivals.
newsitem.headline: "Lost World" tramples on U.S. box office rivals.

text.p: "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" easily topped the U.S. box office for the second consecutive weekend, earning more than the rest of the top 10 combined, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

The Steven Spielberg dinosaur romp took home an estimated $32.6 million for the Friday to Sunday period, bringing its total to $140 million. The next nine grossed about $32.0 million altogether, said Exhibitor Relations, which collects the studios' estimates. Final data will be issued on Monday.
Even though its gross dropped by a hefty 55 percent from the equivalent three-day period last weekend, "The Lost World" still averaged a resounding $9,933 from 3,282 screens.

Universal Pictures expects the movie to earn at least $275 million at the domestic box office. Its first real competition begins next weekend with the arrival of the Nicolas Cage action movie, "Con Air."

"The Lost World" made its foreign premiere in Australia at the weekend, and the Variety trade paper said it looks likely to top the four-day haul of US$3.7 million generated by its 1993 predecessor, "Jurassic Park."
Universal is a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd..
Holding in second this weekend was the Meg Ryan/Matthew Broderick romantic comedy, "Addicted To Love," with $6.4 million. The movie's 10-day total stands at $20.3 million.

The top 10 contained three new entries, none of which performed strongly. "Gone Fishin'," a comedy starring Joe Pesci and Danny Glover, opened in third with about $5.5 million and a $2,988 per-screen average. The Michael Richards/Jeff Daniels comedy "Trial and Error" was fourth with $5.0 million and a $2,176 average. "'Til There Was You," a romantic comedy starring Jeanne Tripplehorn and Dylan McDermott, debuted in 10th with $1.3 million and a $1,726 average.

According to a poll by Variety, critics were generally underwhelmed by both "Trial and Error" and "'Til There Was You." Walt Disney Co. did not screen "Gone Fishin'" for critics, and made up its own advertising blurbs.
Rounding out the top five was the Bruce Willis sci-fi picture ,"The Fifth Element," which earned $4.0 million. After four weekends, it has earned about $51.5 million.

"Addicted To Love" is released by Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc.. "Trial and Error" is released by Time Warner's New Line Cinema, a unit of Time Warner. "'Til There Was You" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.. "The Fifth Element" is released by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp..
